title: Report space reclaimed when a closed job's build cache is deleted
summary: Closing already calls StateDir::clean_job, which silently removes the job directory (including its 11-12 GB target) on some paths. The change makes cleanup cover every closing path, including a close of an interrupted job, report bytes reclaimed, and stop swallowing removal errors; sharing one target directory is evaluated against the checks and recorded as a decision (expected: not adopted). Audience: the Athena operator who ran out of disk.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for each closing path and removal failure; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria assert directory gone and byte count reported, not that a function exists.
Covers all closing paths and error cases instead of the one that surfaced.
Shared-target alternative written down in decisions.md with evidence.
One focused change to cleanup and reporting.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: stop closed jobs from leaving 11-12 GB caches that fill the disk; audience is the Athena operator and the verifier reading output and tests.

Reading of the code: clean_job (state.rs) is already called after close_with, close_dispatched, land_or_block (non-blocked), retry_landing, but it ignores errors, reports nothing, and is skipped when an earlier step errors (e.g. commit out of disk), so leftovers persist.
Sharing one target directory is considered but not adopted by default: review 2 R14 shows a shared dir reuses another job's stale test binaries; per-job isolation is deliberate (D46).
Deleting caches of already-closed historical jobs on this machine is an operational action, not a code deliverable; optionally a sweep could be added but is not assumed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test creates a job directory containing a target/ tree of known size, closes the job through each closing path (landed, failed, rejected, abandoned, interrupted-then-`athena close`, closed while blocked), and asserts the job directory no longer exists and the reported reclaimed byte count equals the known size. Run: cargo test.
The closing line shown to the user (athena go / close output) states the space reclaimed in human units, e.g. 'reclaimed 11.4 GB'; a job with nothing to remove reports no failure.
If removal of the job directory fails, the user sees a warning naming the path rather than silent success (test with an unremovable path or injected error). Run: cargo test.
A job that is still running or blocked keeps its directory; cleanup runs only after the closing commit succeeds. Run: cargo test.

docs/decisions.md records the shared-target-directory question with alternatives and the evidence (docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-review-2.md R14: a shared target dir executed another job's test binaries), and the decision taken; the per-job CARGO_TARGET_DIR in athena.toml stays unless the decision says otherwise.
cargo test, cargo clippy with warnings denied, and cargo fmt --check all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that closing a job deletes its build cache and reports space reclaimed.

out_of_scope: Switching to a shared or persistent cross-job CARGO_TARGET_DIR
Manually deleting directories on the operator's machine
Fixing the land --pr head-checking behavior of job 20261019-013306-zvmr
Capping disk use during a running job
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than reference: touches several closing paths plus a design decision entry.
